title: Product overview, PRD, roadmap & pricing: Redwood Optimize v3 (Q2 2026)
author: Priya Natarajan
content:
Summary
-------
This document consolidates the product overview, high-level PRD and requirements, design principles, roadmap and themes, pricing and packaging guidance, and release notes for Redwood Optimize v3 (internal product name: optimize-v3). Redwood Optimize is Redwood Inference’s toolkit for cost and performance optimization across hosted, dedicated and private deployments. v3 focuses on workload-aware quantization recommendations, adaptive batching controls, integrated A/B evaluation pipelines, and a simplified pricing model for enterprise customers.

Audience
--------
Primary: product managers, engineering leads (serving runtime, infra, applied-ml), sales engineering, solutions engineering, and customer success. Secondary: marketing, finance, and legal for packaging and compliance review.

Goals (north star)
------------------
- Reduce per-token cost by 25% on median workloads without degrading P95 latency beyond SLA.
- Make quantization and batching recommendations non-invasive and reversible for production teams.
- Provide standardized evaluation pipelines to detect quality regressions with a false-positive rate < 5% on curated prompt sets.
- Launch a clear enterprise pricing tier with commit discounts for Dedicated customers and a usage-based hosted tier.

Scope for v3 (what's in and out)
-------------------------------
In scope:
- Automated quantization profile suggestions per model/workload (INT8 and dynamic INT4 previews).
- Adaptive batching controller with region-aware routing for latency-sensitive routes.
- Integrated A/B evaluation harness tied to Redwood Console for quality monitoring and rollback triggers.
- New pricing SKU: Optimize Enterprise (monthly seat + committed throughput discount).

Out of scope:
- New model training or fine-tuning tooling.
- Major changes to serving runtime kernel selection (minor tuning only).

High-level product requirements (PRD)
------------------------------------
1) Recommendation Engine
- Requirement: For each customer route, generate quantization and batching recommendations that estimate cost savings and expected latency impact.
- Inputs: model metadata (architecture, size, tokenization), historical request distribution (sequence length, concurrency), and observed latency percentiles.
- Outputs: ranked recommendation list with estimated monthly savings, risk level (low/medium/high), and confidence score.
- Acceptance criteria: recommendations correct (within 10%) on synthetic benchmark suite for 90% of test cases.

2) Adaptive Batching Controller
- Requirement: Controller should dynamically tune batch size and max wait time to meet per-route latency SLOs while increasing throughput.
- Controls: min_batch_size, max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, latency_target_ms, cold_start_penalty.
- Safety: Must support canary deployment, automatic fallback to previous config after 3 consecutive SLO violations.
- Acceptance criteria: median throughput improvement >= 1.3x on representative customer traces without violating configured SLOs.

3) A/B Evaluation Pipeline
- Requirement: Provide first-class integrations that run A/B comparisons for any recommendation applied (quantization/batching), measure quality regressions using user-provided prompt sets and metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, embedding similarity, custom evals).
- Orchestration: evaluation jobs can be scheduled in Console, with artifact storage and diffed metrics stored for 90 days (configurable).
- Acceptance criteria: automated alert when quality metric delta exceeds threshold; evaluation latency for a 1k-prompt run < 60 minutes on Dedicated capacity.

4) Pricing & Packaging
- Requirement: A clear set of SKUs for Optimize v3: Optimize Pro (hosted pay-as-you-go), Optimize Enterprise (committed Dedicated discounts + support), and Optimize On-prem (private deployment license).
- Requirements: Provide price examples and cost calculator integrated in Console.
- Acceptance criteria: Pricing pages published and legal-approved; cost calculator accuracy within 7% of billing records for sample workloads.

Design specifications (high level)
--------------------------------
Architecture overview:
- Recommendation engine is a stateless microservice that consumes aggregated telemetry (Kafka topic: metrics.optimize.v3) and model metadata from the model registry. It outputs recommended configs to a config-service (versioned).
- Adaptive controller runs as part of the serving control plane and subscribes to per-route telemetry streams. It exposes a dry-run mode and a policy API for rollouts.
- A/B evaluation leverages existing eval-harness (applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness) with added orchestration glue to store results in the Console metrics DB.

Key design choices and trade-offs:
- Quantization preview is non-destructive: optimized weights are stored as separate model variants and only used after explicit customer rollout. This minimizes risk but increases storage footprint.
- Controller uses conservative hysteresis to avoid oscillation; this favors stability over maximum short-term throughput.

API & CLI examples
------------------
- Example recommendation fetch (REST):

GET /api/v1/optimize/recommendations?route_id=prod-chat&window=30d
Response: 200 {"recommendations": [{"id":"rec-123","type":"quantization","estimated_savings":"15%","risk":"low"}]}

- Apply recommendation (dry-run):

POST /api/v1/optimize/apply
Body: {"recommendation_id":"rec-123","route_id":"prod-chat","mode":"dry_run"}

Rollout and safety controls
---------------------------
- All recommendations must support: dry_run, canary (5-25% traffic), full rollout, and automatic rollback.
- Rollback triggers: >3 SLO breaches within 10 minutes or user-specified quality regression detected by A/B pipeline.

Operational SLOs and telemetry
------------------------------
- Recommendation engine availability: 99.9% (monthly).
- Recommendation latency: 95% < 2s for single-route queries.
- Controller decision latency: changes applied within 5s of policy decision under normal load.
- Metrics: per-route token cost, P50/P95 latency, batch size distribution, recommendation adoption rate, evaluation pass/fail rate.

Roadmap & themes (Q4 2025 — Q4 2026)
------------------------------------
Q4 2025: Launch alpha of recommendation engine with manual adoption flows.
Q1 2026: Adaptive batching controller private beta with 3 pilot customers.
Q2 2026: Public launch of Optimize v3 (quantization suggestions + A/B evaluation) — this release.
Q3 2026: Integrations with third-party KMS and extended on-prem packaging.
Q4 2026: Auto-suggested model variant selection and cross-region cost-aware routing for recommendations.

Prioritization rationale
------------------------
- Customer feedback indicates highest ROI for batching + quantization combo; customers reported 20–40% cost reductions when applied safely.
- A/B evaluation is required to unlock confidence and adoption at enterprise scale.

Pricing and packaging notes
--------------------------
Pricing SKUs (summary):
- Optimize Pro (hosted): pay-as-you-go, charged as percentage reduction share model + $0.002 per recommendation execution. Intended for self-serve customers.
- Optimize Enterprise (Dedicated/private): base monthly subscription $5,000 + committed throughput tier discounts (10% discount at $50k/month, 20% at $150k/month). Includes premium support and extended retention for evaluations.
- Optimize On-prem: perpetual license + annual support fee; pricing quoted per-customer.

Cost calculator (Console feature):
- Console shows estimated savings using historical tokens and selected recommendations. Calculation steps are shown to customers and can be exported as CSV for procurement.

Billing & metering
------------------
- Metering events: recommendation_executions, evaluation_jobs_runtime_hours, metered_saved_tokens (estimated).
- Billing will use conservative "estimated_saved_tokens" with guardrails; finance will reconcile estimates at month-end with actual observed delta; adjustments go into next invoice.

Release notes (v3.0) – public launch summary (2026-03-18)
--------------------------------------------------------
Highlights:
- Recommendation engine: per-route quantization and batching suggestions with confidence scores.
- Adaptive batching controller: early-stage rollout support and latency-aware tuning.
- A/B evaluation integration: evaluate quality impact of config changes before full rollout.
- New Optimize Enterprise SKU and Console cost calculator.

Notable bug fixes and caveats:
- Fixed a race condition where recommendations could be re-applied on stale telemetry (fixed in 3.0.1).
- Quantization previews currently support a subset of model families (GPT-style and LLaMA derivatives). Broader architecture support planned for Q3 2026.
- Storage footprint for model variants may increase up to 25% for customers using quantization previews — we provide cleanup tools.

Telemetry and monitoring changes for launch
-----------------------------------------
- New dashboards: Console > Optimize > Adoption shows per-customer adoption and savings.
- Alerts: recommendation-failure-rate > 1% for 15 minutes triggers pager to eng-platform oncall.

Rollout plan and owners
-----------------------
- Product owner: Priya Natarajan (product).
- Engineering leads: Ethan Morales (serving-runtime), Sofia Alvarez (applied-ml), Kenji Yamamoto (eng-platform).
- Solutions & sales engineering: lead by Maria Gomez.
- GTM launch coordinator: Alex Chen.

Rollout phases:
1) Internal dogfooding (2 weeks). Owners: product + applied-ml.
2) Alpha with 3 pilot customers (4 weeks) — engineering oncall support required.
3) Private beta (8 weeks) — expand to 10 customers, integrate billing hooks.
4) Public launch (2026-03-18) — marketing, docs, and full Console rollout.

Post-launch metrics to track
--------------------------
- Adoption rate: fraction of eligible routes with at least one applied recommendation (target 15% in 90 days).
- Median cost savings per-adopted-route (target 25%).
- Quality regression rate per evaluation run (target < 5%).
- Number of automatic rollbacks triggered per 1k rollouts (target < 5).

Open decisions & risk register
-----------------------------
- Decision: use conservative default recommendation thresholds to minimize false positives (approved 2025-10-20).
- Risk: customers with highly safety-sensitive prompts may require longer evaluation windows; mitigations: longer canary periods and manual review.
- Risk: billing reconciliation complexity — mitigation: finance-led reconciliation job and transparent cost export.
